statement: In \(\triangle ABC\), let \(D\) be the foot of the altitude from \(A\) to \(BC\). A circle centered at \(D\) with radius \(AD\) meets lines \(AB\) and \(AC\) at \(P\) and \(Q\) respectively. Show that \(\triangle AQP \sim \triangle ABC\).

In boxes labeled \(0, 1, 2, \ldots\) we place integers by the rules: if \(p\) is prime, place it in box 1; if \(a\) is in box \(m_a\) and \(b\) in box \(m_b\), then \(ab\) is in box \(am_b + bm_a\). Find all positive integers \(n\) placed in box \(n\).
Let \(a, b, c > 0\) with \(abc = 1\). Show that \(\dfrac{a^3}{a^3+2} + \dfrac{b^3}{b^3+2} + \dfrac{c^3}{c^3+2} \geq 1\) and \(\dfrac{1}{a^3+2} + \dfrac{1}{b^3+2} + \dfrac{1}{c^3+2} \leq 1\).

Let \(n > 1\) be odd and \(a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n\) be distinct reals with maximum \(M\) and minimum \(m\). Show that signs \(\pm\) can be chosen for \(s = \pm a_1 \pm a_2 \pm \cdots \pm a_n\) such that \(m < s < M\).

Consider triangle \(ABC\) and point \(M\) on side \(BC\). Let \(P\) be the intersection of the perpendiculars from \(M\) to \(AB\) and from \(B\) to \(BC\), and \(Q\) the intersection of the perpendiculars from \(M\) to \(AC\) and from \(C\) to \(BC\). Show that \(PQ \perp AM\) if and only if \(M\) is the midpoint of \(BC\).

At a party with \(n\) people, among any 4 people there are either 3 who all know each other or 3 who are mutually strangers. Show that the \(n\) people can be separated into two rooms so that everyone in one room knows each other and no two people in the other room know each other.
